companyDescription: AI Photonics · POET Optical Interposer™ platform integrates electronics + photonics on a single chip — enabling 800G optical engines for hyperscale data center AI infrastructure
priceNote: Down ~35% from $15.48 June 4 high on PFIC class action lawsuits; Malaysia 800G ramp Q3 is the recovery catalyst
summary: POET's Optical Interposer platform targets the 800G+ data center AI upgrade cycle — a structurally large opportunity. Near-term legal overhang (PFIC class action lawsuits filed June 2026) and Canadian domicile issues suppress US institutional buying, but Malaysia 800G engine ramp in Q3 2026 remains the key re-rating catalyst if execution delivers.

catalysts.name: Q2 Earnings + Malaysia 800G Ramp Confirmation
catalysts.description: August 19 earnings will reveal first 800G optical engine shipment data from Malaysia; company targets 30,000+ engines shipped in 2026. Q3 ramp is the bullish thesis inflection.

catalysts.name: Malaysia High-Volume Production Go-Live
catalysts.description: POET advancing manufacturing readiness in Malaysia for high-volume 800G optical engines in Q3 2026. Successful production validation = fundamental de-risking.

catalysts.name: PFIC Lawsuit Resolution
catalysts.description: Multiple class action suits allege POET misrepresented its PFIC tax status (April 1–27, 2026). Lead plaintiff deadline June 29. Overhang on US institutional buying until resolved.

risks: PFIC class action lawsuits create legal overhang and suppress US institutional buying pressure
Canadian domicile means US investors face adverse PFIC tax treatment — structural demand headwind
Single analyst coverage (Northland $7 PT) — limited Wall Street visibility
Production ramp execution risk: any delays in Malaysia 800G shipments invalidate the bull thesis
CEO NDA violation allegations may jeopardize key business partnerships
Small-cap (~$350M) with minimal revenue — dependent on ramp materializing in H2 2026

analystTargets.note: Dec 2024 — outdated; stock ran above PT then retraced on lawsuit

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed held at 3.50–3.75% on June 17; dot plot now leans toward one 2026 hike. July 29 FOMC next.
macroRisk.inflationNote: CPI next July 14; hot print could push hike probability higher and compress growth multiples.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: AI photonics hardware benefits from capex spend even in higher-rate environment, but small-cap growth names compress on rate fears. POET's Canadian status adds FX risk.
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM macro risk: rate hike probability (30%) + small-cap multiple compression are headwinds, but AI data center capex remains structurally robust as direct demand driver.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE — 5% max position; await August earnings for 800G ramp confirmation before adding. PFIC cloud limits institutional support.

catalystSpot.preRunup: AI photonics names typically run 15-25% pre-production milestone announcements as spec buyers position ahead of ramp confirmations. POET ran from ~$5 to $15 in early 2026 on AI photonics hype before lawsuit reversal.

postWin.note: Comparable optical component ramp confirmations (e.g., II-VI/Coherent 400G volume in Dec 2021) drove +30-50% moves over 4-6 weeks. POET's 800G at smaller scale suggests similar % magnitude.

postLose.note: When MACOM (MACOM) production delays hit in 2019, stock fell 35% over 2 months. POET ramp miss would likely trigger similar de-rating.

spotSizing.reason: High conviction on AI photonics thesis, but PFIC legal risk + limited coverage = 5% max. Binary ramp outcome warrants small starter position.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below $7.50 signals lawsuit settlement costs + ramp delay = thesis break

stopPostCatalyst.note: If earnings miss on 800G shipments, exit immediately — don't wait for recovery

comparableCases.note: Ciena confirmed first high-volume 400G shipments to hyperscalers; stock ran +28% in 10 days. POET's 800G analog is structurally similar but smaller scale.
II-VI (now Coherent) 400G volume delivery to hyperscalers drove re-rating. Direct comparable to POET's Malaysia 800G ramp.
MACOM optical component production delays caused -35% selloff. This is the downside case if POET's Q3 Malaysia ramp slips.
